sheet-75-1.description: The lower half of the title sheet of the 1905 Toms River atlas, drawn at 60 feet to an inch, showing the north end of the village along North Main Street. North Main Street runs down the left side of the part and Seward Avenue along its foot, with a short stub of Thomas Street leaving Seward Avenue at the lower right. The part covers block 54 on the west side of North Main Street and the deep lots of block 1A north of Seward Avenue, which is the edge of the built-up village at this date. Only scattered frame dwellings are drawn, most of one and a half to two and a half stories, with stables, hen houses and a work shop behind them; much of the area is open lots. Water pipes are shown in North Main Street (a 6 inch pipe of 1897) and Seward Avenue (a 4 inch pipe of 1898), with fire hydrants at the corners, and a scale bar is printed at the foot of the sheet. The upper half of the sheet, which is not part of this annotation, carries the title, a key map of the whole village at a much smaller scale, the legend, notes on the water facilities and fire department, and three small insets of outlying properties: the Toms River and Island Heights Electric Light and Power Company station, the Fraunce Brothers boat yard and the Toms River Water Company pumping station. Those insets show no street junction and were not georeferenced.
notes: The part is placed from two hand-picked junctions only (a helmert fit); its fitted scale is about 4 percent smaller than the other sheets'.
Key map, legend and three single-property insets on the same sheet are not part of this annotation.

Title sheet with a key map of the whole village (about 400 ft to an inch, not georeferenced), the key, and three single-property insets (Toms River & Island Heights Electric Light & Power Co's station 3/4 mile W of Court House; Fraunce Bros. boat yard 3/4 mile SSW; Toms River Water Co. pumping station 1 mile W), none with a street junction. Part 1: strip along N. Main St and Seward Av (block 54/1A) at 60 ft to an inch. Scale 60 ft.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Toms River Water Co. pumping station, 1 mile W of Court House (single property, no street junction).

sheet-76-1.description: Residential blocks on the east side of North Main Street in the north part of the village of Toms River, drawn at 60 feet to an inch. The part is bounded by North Main Street on the west, Seward Avenue along the top edge, Thomas Street and the lots beyond it on the east, and Union Street at the foot. Dayton Avenue and Dover Street cross it from North Main Street, and Hires Street runs diagonally from Dayton Avenue south-west to Union Street, cutting the blocks into irregular lots. Stubs of Colfax Street, Broad Street and Messenger Street are lettered on the far side of North Main Street, where sheet 77 continues. The blocks, numbered 57, 58, 59 and 1A, carry detached frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half stories with stables, wagon houses, wood houses and hen houses in the rear yards; several large lots, especially between Dayton Avenue and Dover Street and east of Hires Street, are drawn empty. Water pipes of 1897 and 1900 are shown in the streets with hydrants at most corners. The lower right corner of the sheet is a separate inset of South Main Street and Dover Road south of the river, which is a different place and is annotated as part 2. A compass rose and the scale bar are printed in the left margin and at the foot.
notes: Hires Street is today's Hyers Street.
The part is drawn turned about 11 degrees: North Main Street runs straight up the page.

N. Main St to Thomas St, Seward Av to Union St (Dayton Av, Dover St, Hires St = modern Hyers Street). Part 1 main map; part 2 inset in the lower right: S. Main St and Dover Road south of the river, drawn at another rotation. Scale 60 ft.

sheet-76-2.description: A small inset in the lower right corner of sheet 76, drawn at 60 feet to an inch and set apart by a heavy border, showing a stretch of South Main Street on the south side of the Toms River, where it meets Dover Road. South Main Street runs down the left side of the inset and Dover Road leaves it diagonally toward the lower right; the junction itself lies just below the bottom edge of the sheet. The inset has its own north arrow, turned away from that of the main map, and carries the block numbers 2A and 3A, continuing the numbering of the strip of South Main Street that is drawn in insets on sheets 82 and 78. The ground is thinly built: a few frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half stories face South Main Street, with small outbuildings and stables behind them, and two or three small buildings stand along Dover Road. The large sheet number 82 at the top of the inset shows that South Main Street continues northward on sheet 82. Street widths of 40 feet for South Main Street and 30 feet for Dover Road are lettered, and no water pipes are shown, which places it outside the village water system of 1905. The inset is not connected on the ground to the rest of sheet 76, which shows the north end of the village around North Main Street.
notes: Placed from one junction (South Main Street / Dover Road, centre just off the sheet) with an assumed scale and the rotation measured from its drawn lines: low confidence.
Dover Road here is matched to today's Dover Road east of South Main Street.

N. Main St to Thomas St, Seward Av to Union St (Dayton Av, Dover St, Hires St = modern Hyers Street). Part 1 main map; part 2 inset in the lower right: S. Main St and Dover Road south of the river, drawn at another rotation. Scale 60 ft.

sheet-77-1.description: The left half of sheet 77, separated from the right half by a heavy vertical line, showing the west side of North Main Street from north of Colfax Street to Messenger Street in the village of Toms River, at 60 feet to an inch. North Main Street runs down the right edge of the part, with short stubs of Dayton Avenue, Dover Street and Union Street lettered on its east side. Colfax Street, Broad Street and Messenger Street run west from it, and Park Street forms the west boundary of the lower blocks. Block 54 at the top is mostly open ground crossed by a ravine, with duck houses and hen coops; blocks 55 and 56 below are lined with frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half stories facing North Main Street and the cross streets, with sheds, stables and storage buildings at the rear. The First Baptist Church and its annex stand on the south side of Broad Street, and a brick dwelling stands at the corner of North Main and Messenger Streets. Water pipes of 1897 and 1900 run in North Main Street and the cross streets, with hydrants at the corners. The area east of North Main Street on this half of the sheet is left to sheet 76, whose number is printed there. A compass rose stands on the dividing line and the scale bar at the foot.
notes: The sheet is drawn as two strips side by side; this part is the northern one.

Two parts side by side, divided by a heavy line: part 1 (left) N. Main St west side from Colfax St to Messenger St, with Broad St and Park St; part 2 (right) Park St to N. Main St, Messenger St to Snyder Av (Lien St). Scale 60 ft.

sheet-77-2.description: The right half of sheet 77, set off from the left half by a heavy vertical line, showing the blocks between Park Street and North Main Street from Messenger Street south to Snyder Avenue in the village of Toms River, at 60 feet to an inch. It continues the left half southward: Messenger Street crosses the top, Lien Street the middle and Snyder Avenue the lower part, with Park Street on the west and North Main Street along the east edge. Blocks 50, 51 and 53 are filled with frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half stories, many with stables, carriage houses, wood sheds, hen houses and storage buildings behind them; a pigeon house, a slaughter house, a corn crib and the ruin of a barn are lettered in the rear yards. A tenement building stands near Snyder Avenue. Below Snyder Avenue, block 1 is largely open, and the business buildings of sheet 81 appear in the lower right corner, where North Main Street approaches the river. Water pipes of 1897 and 1900 are shown in Lien Street, Snyder Avenue and North Main Street, with hydrants. A strip at the left edge carries the number of sheet 76 and blank ground belonging to the other half of the sheet.
notes: Snyder Avenue follows today's Snyder Street and the east end of Irons Street; its junction with North Main Street was not detected.
Lien Street as drawn lies a few metres from today's line; its junctions carry 1.5 to 2 m residuals.

Two parts side by side, divided by a heavy line: part 1 (left) N. Main St west side from Colfax St to Messenger St, with Broad St and Park St; part 2 (right) Park St to N. Main St, Messenger St to Snyder Av (Lien St). Scale 60 ft.

sheet-78-1.description: Residential and civic blocks east of North Main Street in the village of Toms River, drawn at 60 feet to an inch. North Main Street runs diagonally from the upper left to the foot of the sheet, where it meets Washington Street; Union Street and Walton Street run north-east from it to Hires Street, which crosses the sheet from top to bottom with a pronounced jog; Sheriff Street runs east from Hires Street to Horner Street, and Washington Street forms the bottom edge. Stubs of Messenger Street, Lien Street and Snyder Avenue are lettered on the west side of North Main Street. Block 52 between Union and Walton Streets is closely built with frame dwellings and stables. Below Walton Street the large block 6 is mostly open, with a dilapidated old Catholic church near Hires Street. The Toms River School, a brick building with hot air heat and electric lights, stands on Horner Street near the right edge, and a row of small shops and offices, including an ice cream and harness shop, plumbers and tinsmiths, a printing office and a carpenter, lines the north side of Washington Street. Court House Alley leaves the end of Sheriff Street at the right edge. Two separately bordered insets cut into the sheet: The Granmoor Farm of John P. Haines at the top right, and South Main Street with the railroad station at the lower left; they are annotated separately or not at all.
notes: Hires Street is today's Hyers Street; its junctions with Union and Walton Streets disagree with the rest of the sheet by 15 to 20 m and were left out.
Horner Street north of Washington Street is today's Courthouse Lane.
The four junctions along Washington Street and Horner Street were hand-picked; the detector paired the wrong lines there.
Toms River School stood on Horner Street, north of Washington Street.

N. Main St, Union, Walton, Hires (Hyers Street) and Sheriff Sts to Washington St; Toms River School. Part 1 main map; part 2 inset top right: The Granmoor Farm (John P. Haines), 3/4 mile E of Court House, no street; part 3 inset lower left: S. Main St and Mill St south of the river with the Penn. & L.B. R.R. station, drawn at another rotation. Scale 60 ft.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The Granmoor Farm (John P. Haines), 3/4 mile E of Court House (single property, no street junction).

sheet-78-3.description: An inset in the lower left corner of sheet 78, set off by a heavy border and drawn at 60 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, showing South Main Street on the south side of the Toms River where Mill Street leaves it toward the east. It is a different place from the rest of sheet 78 and continues the strip of South Main Street drawn in the inset on sheet 76, with blocks numbered 1A, 2A and 3A. South Main Street runs diagonally down the left side and Mill Street crosses the lower half from the South Main Street frontage toward the upper right. The Pennsylvania and Long Beach Railroad's Toms River station occupies the ground south of Mill Street, with a water closet, the station building, a pump house and a tank, and the railroad's barn stands on the north side of Mill Street; the tracks themselves run along the lower right edge. The rest of the inset is sparsely built: frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half stories with hen houses and small outbuildings face South Main Street and Mill Street, on large lots with much open ground. No water pipes or hydrants are shown, and the lower right of the inset is marked no exposure. The railroad here is the line toward Barnegat Bay, distinct from the Central Railroad of New Jersey drawn on sheets 81 and 82.
notes: Placed from one detected junction (South Main Street / Mill Street) with an assumed scale and the rotation measured from its drawn lines: low confidence.
The station is the Pennsylvania and Long Beach Railroad's Toms River station; the line is no longer in use.

N. Main St, Union, Walton, Hires (Hyers Street) and Sheriff Sts to Washington St; Toms River School. Part 1 main map; part 2 inset top right: The Granmoor Farm (John P. Haines), 3/4 mile E of Court House, no street; part 3 inset lower left: S. Main St and Mill St south of the river with the Penn. & L.B. R.R. station, drawn at another rotation. Scale 60 ft.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The Granmoor Farm (John P. Haines), 3/4 mile E of Court House (single property, no street junction).

sheet-79.description: The east bank of the Toms River below the village centre, drawn at 60 feet to an inch on a sheet turned so that north points to the upper right. Water Street runs from Allen Street at the top down the length of the sheet, following the river bank on its west side, and Washington Street runs down the right side; Hooper Avenue crosses between them, Curve Street swings from Water Street toward Washington Street in the lower half, and Hadley Avenue meets Washington Street at the lower right. The river, lettered Toms River, fills the left margin, with several small docks and wharves along the bank and a large dwelling with a cupola on the water side of Water Street. Block 60 between Allen Street and Hooper Avenue is closely built with dwellings, storage buildings, sheds and a carriage house, and the Methodist Episcopal Church stands at its Washington Street end. South of Hooper Avenue, St. Joseph Church and its annex for winter services face the avenue, and block 61 below holds large dwellings on deep lots. Below Curve Street block 1A is mostly open ground with a few dwellings, a laundry and a summer house by the river. Water pipes of 1897, 1901 and 1904 are shown in the streets with hydrants. A compass rose and the scale bar are drawn near the river.
notes: Water Street is today's East Water Street.
Curve Street roughly follows today's Caldwell Lane.
The sheet is turned: north points about 73 degrees clockwise from the top.
Water St (modern East Water Street), Allen St, Hooper Av, Washington St, Curve St, along the Toms River; St. Joseph Church, M.E. Church. Sheet turned: north points up-right. Scale 60 ft.

sheet-80-1.description: The county seat blocks of Toms River on the left half of sheet 80, drawn at 60 feet to an inch and separated from the right half by a heavy line; the sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right. Washington Street runs down the left edge, Horner Street across the top and Hooper Avenue across the middle, with Court House Alley running between Horner Street and Hooper Avenue, and Hadley Avenue at the foot. The upper block holds the Ocean County Court House, heated by stoves and lit by electricity, with the brick jail and its kitchen behind it, the Grand Opera House on Horner Street and the Toms River Water Company's tank, 105 feet high, on a lot beside it. The rest of the blocks between Horner Street and Hooper Avenue and south of Hooper Avenue (block 62) are lined with frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half stories with stables and storage buildings at the rear; the lower part of the half sheet, toward Hadley Avenue, is mostly open ground with a few scattered houses. Water pipes, some dated 1897 and 1901, are drawn in Washington Street, Horner Street and Hooper Avenue, with hydrants. A compass rose is printed near the dividing line.
notes: Horner Street here is today's Courthouse Lane; the Horner Street / Washington Street junction was hand-picked.
Placed from two points along Washington Street only (a helmert fit): low confidence.
Ocean County Court House and jail, the Grand Opera House and the water company's tank stand in the upper block.

Two parts divided by a heavy vertical line: part 1 (left) Washington St, Horner St, Court House Alley, Hooper Av, Hadley Av, with the Ocean County Court House and jail; part 2 (right) Washington St southeast of Hadley Av with Duck St, Lexington Av, Clinton Av, Brackenridge Av. Turned sheet: north points up-right. Scale 60 ft.

sheet-80-2.description: The right half of sheet 80, separated from the left half by a heavy vertical line, showing Washington Street east of Hadley Avenue in Toms River at 60 feet to an inch. The half sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right; Washington Street runs diagonally from Hadley Avenue at the top down to the foot of the sheet. Duck Street leaves Washington Street on the west side, Lexington Avenue runs east from it in the middle, Clinton Avenue runs along the upper right edge between Hadley Avenue and Lexington Avenue, and Brackenridge Avenue leaves Washington Street on the west side lower down. Block 63, between Hadley Avenue, Clinton Avenue and Lexington Avenue, is built with frame dwellings of two and two and a half stories and their stables and outbuildings; the blocks south of Lexington Avenue (1A, 2A and 3A) are almost entirely open, with a single dwelling beside Brackenridge Avenue and the Episcopal Church, lit by kerosene oil and heated by hot air, at the foot of the sheet. Water pipes of 1897 are drawn in Washington Street and Lexington Avenue, and the street widths, 50 to 70 feet, are lettered. The area west of the dividing line shows the courthouse blocks, annotated as part 1.
notes: Duck Street is today's Dock Street.
Brackenridge Avenue was not matched to a modern street.
Clinton Avenue junctions are at the sheet edge and were placed from one drawn edge.

Two parts divided by a heavy vertical line: part 1 (left) Washington St, Horner St, Court House Alley, Hooper Av, Hadley Av, with the Ocean County Court House and jail; part 2 (right) Washington St southeast of Hadley Av with Duck St, Lexington Av, Clinton Av, Brackenridge Av. Turned sheet: north points up-right. Scale 60 ft.

sheet-81.description: The business centre of Toms River at the bridge over the Toms River, drawn at 60 feet to an inch on a sheet turned so that north points to the upper right. North Main Street runs across the upper middle of the sheet from Washington Street to the river, where it meets Water Street, Manchester Road and South Main Street; South Main Street crosses the river westward on two iron bridges with an island between them. Water Street runs down the sheet from that junction, with Robbins Street, Horner Street and Allen Street crossing to Washington Street on the right. Both sides of North Main Street are lined with brick and frame stores, offices and halls, including the First National Bank, drug and dry goods stores, a bakery, a barber, billiards and a post office, with the Ocean House and the Riverside House, hotels with their barns, near the bridge. The F. M. Chambers lumber and coal yards with coal bins and lumber sheds lie between North Main and Robbins Streets and below Robbins Street, the A. R. Brant lumber yard and W. P. Kirk's yacht building shop and yacht storage sheds lie along the river, and the Presbyterian Church faces Horner Street. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the river at the upper left, and its railroad station appears at the left edge, where sheet 82 continues. The river is lettered Toms River.
notes: Water Street is today's East Water Street; Manchester Road is today's West Water Street.
Robbins Street as drawn lies 6 to 9 m from today's Robbins Street; it was left out of the fit.
The junctions of North Main Street with Water Street and with Washington Street were hand-picked between building fronts.

Downtown: N. Main St and S. Main St at the river bridge, Water St, Robbins St, Horner St, Allen St, Washington St, Manchester Road; Riverside House, Ocean House, F.M. Chambers lumber, W.P. Kirk yacht builder. Turned sheet: north points up-right. Scale 60 ft.

sheet-82-1.description: South Main Street on the south side of the Toms River, drawn at 60 feet to an inch on the upper part of sheet 82. South Main Street runs straight down the middle from the river at the top to a second arm of the river at the foot of the part; the Turnpike leaves it toward the lower right, and the railroad crosses it near the top, curving east past the railroad station and the freight house. The river, lettered Toms River, wraps around the west side, where A. B. Newbury's lumber, coal, wood, paints, oils and hardware yard fills the ground between South Main Street and the water with lumber sheds, storage buildings, open coal bins, wood piles and a wood sawing shed worked by horse power. Frorer and Yoder's general machine works, with power from a gasoline engine, stands beside the tracks east of the station. Along South Main Street and the Turnpike are frame dwellings, a paints and oils store, a hardware store and shingle storage. Block 10, east of South Main Street and south of the Turnpike, is mostly open. A 4 inch water pipe of 1901 runs in South Main Street with a hydrant at the Turnpike. The lower part of the sheet, below a heavy line, holds two insets of saw mills further south and is not part of this annotation.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked point, the railroad crossing of South Main Street (taken as today's South Main Street / Herflicker Boulevard, which follows the former railroad bed), with assumed scale and rotation: low confidence, about 15 to 20 m.
The Turnpike lies between today's Herflicker Boulevard and Flint Road; its modern name is uncertain.
The railroad is the former Toms River branch of the Central Railroad of New Jersey.

Part 1 (top): S. Main St south of the river with the Turnpike, the R.R. station and the railroad; A.B. Newbury lumber, Frorer & Yoder machine works. Part 2 inset lower left: S. Main St with W.T. Giberson's saw mill. Part 3 inset lower right: E.R. Yoder's saw mill on Van Schoick Road, 1 1/4 mile SW of Court House. Scale 60 ft.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: S. Main Street with W. T. Giberson's saw mill (only junction (Van Schoick Road) at the inset edge, and Van Schoick Road not matched to a modern street; needs identify Van Schoick Road (Center Street or Magnolia Avenue?), then anchor on that junction).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: E. R. Yoder's saw mill on Van Schoick Road, 1 1/4 mile SW of Court House (no street junction; Van Schoick Road not matched to a modern street; needs identify Van Schoick Road and the mill race).
